title: White House Abruptly Pulls ICE Director Nominee After GOP Senator Blocks Hearing
snippet: The White House has withdrawn Oklahoma state trooper Lance Schroyer’s nomination to lead ICE after Senate Homeland Security Chair Rand Paul stalled his confirmation process.
content:
The White House on Thursday officially pulled the nomination of Lance Schroyer to lead U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), following a high-profile roadblock set by Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul (R-Ky.).

Schroyer’s confirmation process ground to a sudden halt after Paul requested that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) hand over key documents regarding an investigation into two federal agents involved in the fatal shooting of two U.S. citizens in Minneapolis earlier this year. While a spokesperson for Paul noted that the senator did not explicitly oppose Schroyer’s appointment, his control over the committee’s schedule effectively shelved the nomination.

An Unconventional Pick Under Fire

Schroyer, an Oklahoma state trooper, was a surprise choice for the top post at ICE. Lacking prior experience at the helm of any major law enforcement agency, his primary connection to the role was his close tie to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. Schroyer previously headed Mullin’s personal security detail before stepping into a senior advisory role at DHS.

Secretary Mullin had repeatedly championed Schroyer, highlighting his track record in building specialized units within the Oklahoma Highway Patrol and fostering local law enforcement partnerships with federal immigration officials. However, the nomination met swift resistance from immigration hardliners who doubted Schroyer possessed the administrative experience required to command a complex agency of ICE's size—or the political capital to clear a divided Senate.

A Prolonged Leadership Vacuum

Schroyer’s abrupt exit ensures that ICE’s decade-long streak without a Senate-confirmed leader will continue. The agency has not had a permanent, confirmed director at the helm since 2014, reflecting the deeply polarizing nature of federal immigration enforcement in recent years.

For now, Acting ICE Director David Venturella will continue to run the agency. Venturella, an ally of White House border czar Tom Homan, was legally permitted to serve indefinitely while Schroyer’s nomination was pending. With the nomination officially withdrawn, federal law now triggers a 210-day limit on Venturella’s acting tenure unless the White House puts forward a new candidate. However, insiders note that Venturella could face his own steep confirmation battle due to his past executive work for GEO Group, one of the nation's largest private detention contractors.
